cable car: a vehicle hung from a moving cable that carries people up a slope
call it a day: to stop working because you have done enough
call off: to cancel something that was planned
calm before the storm: a quiet time that comes just before trouble or hard work
camel in the room: an obvious problem that everyone avoids mentioning
carbon footprint: the amount of carbon dioxide your actions add to the air
carbon neutral: adding no more carbon dioxide to the air than you remove
carry out: to do a task, plan or order
carry out research: to do a planned study to find facts
carry-on baggage: the small bag you keep with you on a plane
cash flow: the movement of money into and out of a business
catch someone's eye: to make someone look at you or at what you are showing
chair a meeting: to lead a meeting and keep it to its agenda
cheap / inexpensive / affordable: costing little, or within what you can pay
check in: to register your arrival at a hotel, airport or event
check-in desk: the counter where you register at a hotel or airport
check-out: the act of paying and leaving a hotel
checked baggage: suitcases handed to the airline and carried in the hold
choose / select / opt for: to decide which one you want, from a range of choices
clean out: to empty a place and clean it thoroughly
clean the house: to tidy and wash the rooms where you live
climate change: the long-term shift in the earth's weather caused by warming
close attention: careful watching or listening, with nothing missed
close friend: someone you know well and trust
code-switching: changing between two languages or styles while you speak
come across: to meet or find something by chance
come home: to return to the place where you live
come to terms with: to accept something difficult and learn to live with it
come up with: to think of an idea, plan or solution
compound interest: interest paid on both your money and the interest it has already earned
connecting flight: a second plane that continues your journey after the first
control group: the people in an experiment who are not given the treatment
cope with: to deal successfully with something difficult
corner shop: a small local shop selling everyday things
credit card: a plastic card used to buy things and pay later
credit score: a number showing how safely you repay borrowed money
cut short: to end something earlier than planned
cut to the chase: to get to the important point without delay
cutting board: a flat board you chop food on
dark blue: a deep blue, close to navy
dark gray: a deep gray, close to charcoal
dark green: a deep green, close to forest green
data usage: the amount of mobile internet you have used
de facto: existing in fact, even if not officially recognized
dear sir or madam: the polite way to open a formal letter when you do not know the name
declutter: to remove the things you do not need from a place
deep sleep: the heavy stage of sleep when the body repairs itself
derive from: to come from, or to get something from a source
diamonds in the rough: people or things with real value hidden under a poor surface
difficult / hard / challenging: needing effort, or testing your ability
direct flight: a flight that goes to your destination without a change of plane
do business: to buy, sell or trade with people
do research: to study a subject carefully to find new facts
do the dishes: to wash the plates and pans after a meal
do the shopping: to go out and buy the food and goods you need
do the washing up: to wash the plates and pans after a meal
double room: a hotel room with a bed for two people
down to earth: practical, honest and not pretending to be important
draw a blank: to get no answer or result, however hard you try
draw a conclusion: to decide what something means after looking at the facts
draw a distinction: to point out the difference between two things
drift apart: to slowly become less close to someone
drop by: to visit someone briefly, usually without planning
drop out: to leave school, a course or a race before finishing
duct tape: a strong wide sticky tape used for repairs
due diligence: the careful checking done before a deal or decision
easy / simple / straightforward: not difficult, not complicated, or clear to follow
emergency exit: the door meant for leaving a building quickly in danger
emergency services: the police, fire and medical teams you call in a crisis
emoji: a small picture keyboard character used to show feeling
excess baggage: luggage over the weight or number your ticket allows
exchange rate: how much one currency is worth in another
extra large: larger than the usual large size
